why: the reseal door could not REPROVE cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/proofs/test_a_beat_costs_what_changed.py inside its 120s budget — it timed out. This is the door's impatience, not the proof's verdict, so no seal was written and no repair was bounded: the standing record is untouched and the component stays red at rung 1 because its fingerprint moved. The red was measured with faulthandler, not guessed: the beat's codemother pulse (groundloop/pulse.py on_pulse -> watch.on_commit -> _escalate_to_hex -> bus.request timeout=60s) processes every commit since ~/.cairn/devices/codemother/0/watch/last_seen_head.json synchronously inside the beat, one 60s bus request per area with no reply under the tester's netns; the 56-file artifact-door commit 250a65a (and then a38204e) made the first beat exceed the seal timeout. Once codemother's head caught up to HEAD the proof ran at 92s. The latent cause — a blocking escalation inside a heartbeat — is a design question for Akien, not patched here.
